dish_name: Skillet Pork Chops with Mushroom Gravy
instructions: Put the 1 1/2 cups rice in a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil over high heat.
Cover it, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you're ready to eat.
Meanwhile, pat the 4 pork chops dry with paper towels. Mix the 1/2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper in a small bowl and sprinkle it over both sides of the chops.

Heat a large skillet over medium high heat and add 2 tbsp of the butter. When the foam settles, add the chops and leave them alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until the undersides are deep golden and let go of the pan.

Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. You're cooking them to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest chop there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest one: it's done when the juices run clear and the center is only faintly pink. Transfer them to a plate.

Turn the heat to medium and add the remaining 2 tbsp butter to the same pan. Add the mushrooms and the last 1/4 tsp salt and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're golden and their liquid has cooked off.
Add the garlic and the 1 1/2 tsp Dijon and stir for about 1 minute, until the garlic smells sweet.
Sprinkle the 2 tbsp flour over the mushrooms and stir for 1 minute, until there's no dry flour left.

Slowly pour in the 2 cups broth, whisking as you go, and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Let it simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Put the chops back in the pan with any juices from the plate. Spoon the gravy over them and heat for 1 minute.
Taste the gravy. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the chops and mushroom gravy with the rice.
method_notes: Every version sears the chops first, cooks the mushrooms in the same pan, stirs in flour and whisks in broth for the gravy, then puts the chops back to warm through. Recipe Girl (the lead) seasons the chops with paprika and uses butter, garlic and a little Dijon with 2 cups of broth, while Food Network Kitchen dusts bone-in chops in flour and finishes the gravy with scallions, parsley and sour cream, and Taste of Home bakes floured chops under a milk gravy for 50 minutes. None of the pages had 20 ratings (Taste of Home shows 30 reviews, a reviewCount, not a ratingCount, and no rating) and RecipeTin Eats has only a standalone mushroom sauce, so the lead is the read version closest to a one-pan weeknight skillet. This follows the lead with the rice it suggests serving alongside.
